Mthatha Police Stations' Investigation

By: Sipha Kema | Paid

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Gruesome crimes continue to escalate in Mthatha, with the police in the middle.

Unique Selling Point:
Mthatha, a place of crime and fear. A small city where murders, rapes and gender-based violence have
become the norm and it seems it’s not going to change anytime soon, with police now part of criminal
syndicates and corruption.
For years the people of Mthatha have been complaining about the corruption and incompetence at
Madiera and Central Police Stations in Mthatha. Murder dockets and files going missing, rape cases have
gone cold…the unspoken yet known truth, the police officers at the two stations are selling case
dockets. This interferes with victims ever getting justice, no docket? No case. Suspects walk away, free.
These two police stations have come under the spotlight following Namhla Mtwa’s death, after
allegations of bribery and corruption were made against the two embattled stations. Namhla Mtwa’s
sister revealed that Namhla had reported the abuse she suffered allegedly by her boyfriend, Major
Bhekizulu Mfesane, but Namhla was turned away a number of times or Major would be called by the
police to fetch Namhla. The sister alleged that the police officers were on Major’s payroll. Subsequently,
more and more women came forward about their missing case files, unopened dockets and being
dismissed when going to open a case.
The criminal behaviour of the police in Mthatha, has bred unlawlessness into the city. Minister of Police,
Bheki Cele, has noted Mthatha as one of the hotspots. According to the recent SAPS national crime
stats, Mthatha has one of the highest murder rates, alongside Umlazi in Durban and Plessislaer in
KwaZulu-Natal, surpassing the deadly Delft in the Western Cape. Marches, protests and even Cele
visited the stations, instead the crime stats have worsened.
Several residents have come forward to assist in exposing the corruption that takes place at these police
stations. They have studied how the operation works and who’s who with the middlemen between the
suspects and police officers. It’s time to expose the corruption so the people of Mthatha can hopefully
receive justice.

Further information:
We need to setup a bait and I do have some guys who normally take part in criminal activities who are
willing to go undercover to bribe an officer or the middleman for a case file to disappear. The “suspect”
will first ask how the process works, how much he needs, is this guaranteed? Most of this will use a
hidden camera and cellphones
For case studies, we have one GBV and rape victim who is willing to speak out about the treatment she
received at the police station when she went to open a case. And the perpetrator walking free because

there was no case file. She will tell us about her story but focusing on the injustice she received. Seeing
her perpetrator walking passed her every day.
We have a community leader who wants to see this corruption exposed, we will hide their identity for
their safety. In Mthatha assassinations happen almost everyday in broad daylight.
We will reach out to the Eastern Cape SAPS regarding these known allegations. What has been done
with the investigations into the corruption and bribery allegations? At the EFF March in April 2022,
whilst the Deputy Commissioner accepted the memorandum, Brigadier Kinana requested for all those
with unresolved GBV/Rape cases to send their case numbers…how far with those unresolved cases?
SAPS EC seems nonchalant about the scary crime in the Mthatha, caused by unlawlessness by the police
themselves.
Although we will get a comment from EC SAPS, we will also visit the police station, shoot outside…to get
visuals but also we will be able to see people standing in long queues waiting for help.
